nodes.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, if Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances rather than a negative cycle, then the run charges zero negative-cycle witness reconstruction steps.
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford spends no witness steps when it returns distances

nodes.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, if Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns a reachable negative cycle whose cycle has $c$ edges and whose path from $s$ to the cycle has $q$ edges, then the run charges exactly $n + c + q$ negative-cycle witness reconstruction steps.
nodes.title: Witness cost of a returned negative cycle

nodes.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ charges at most $3n$ negative-cycle witness reconstruction steps.
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford spends at most $3n$ witness steps

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. If Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances $d$, with $\infty$ marking a vertex that has no finite distance, then for every vertex $t$, $d(t) = \infty$ if and only if $t$ is not reachable from $s$ in the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting the weights.
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford leaves exactly the unreachable vertices at infinite distance

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. If Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances $d$, the distance $d(t)$ of a vertex $t$ is a finite integer $\delta$, and $P$ is a walk from $s$ to $t$ along edges of $E$ (vertices may repeat), then $\delta$ is at most the total weight of $P$.
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford distances are lower bounds on walk weights

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. If Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances $d$ and the distance $d(t)$ of a vertex $t$ is a finite integer $\delta$, then there is a walk from $s$ to $t$ along edges of $E$ whose total weight is $\delta$.
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford distances are realized by walks

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. If Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances $d$, with $\infty$ marking a vertex that has no finite distance, together with predecessor edges, then for every vertex $t$, reconstructing a path to $t$ (following predecessor edges back from $t$ for at most $n$ steps until $s$ is reached) fails if…
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford path reconstruction fails exactly at infinite distances

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. Suppose Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances $d$ together with predecessor edges, and that reconstructing a path to a vertex $t$ (following predecessor edges back from $t$ for at most $n$ steps until $s$ is reached) yields the edge sequence $P$. Then $P$ is a walk from $s$ to $t$ along…
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford reconstructed paths are simple and realize the distances

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. Suppose Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances $d$ together with predecessor edges, and the predecessor edge of a vertex $t$ is an edge $e$ from $u$ to $v$ of weight $w$. Then $e$ belongs to $E$, $v = t$, and $d(u)$ and $d(t)$ are both finite with $d(t) = d(u) + w$.
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford predecessor edges are tight

nodes.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ charges exactly $n \cdot |E|$ relaxation checks, where $|E|$ is the length of $E$ counting repeated edges.
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford makes exactly $n \cdot |E|$ relaxation checks

nodes.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ charges exactly $(n - 1) \cdot |E| + |E|$ relaxation checks, where $|E|$ is the length of $E$.
nodes.title: Relaxation checks of Bellman-Ford pass by pass

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances if and only if there is no negative cycle reachable from $s$, that is, no simple path from $s$ to a vertex $b$ together with a nonempty cycle through $b$ along edges of $E$ whose edge sources are pairwise distinct and whose total weight is negative.
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford succeeds exactly when no negative cycle is reachable

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns a reachable negative cycle witness if and only if a negative cycle is reachable from $s$, that is, there are a simple path from $s$ to a vertex $b$ and a nonempty cycle through $b$ along edges of $E$ whose edge sources are pairwise distinct and whose total weight…
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford reports a negative cycle exactly when one is reachable

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. If Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ returns distances together with predecessor edges, then $s$ has no predecessor edge.
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford gives the source no predecessor

nodes.summary: For every list $E$ of weighted edges on $n$ vertices and every source $s$, the total cost of Bellman-Ford run on $E$ from $s$ (its relaxation checks plus its negative-cycle witness reconstruction steps) is at most $4 \cdot n \cdot |E|$, where $|E|$ is the length of $E$.
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford makes at most $4 n |E|$ counted steps

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of integer-weighted directed edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ be a vertex. Bellman–Ford run on $E$ from $s$ starts with distance $d(s) = 0$ and $d(v) = \infty$ for every other vertex $v$, and makes $n - 1$ passes over $E$ followed by one final pass. A pass goes through the edges of $E$ in list order, charging one relaxation check per edge occurrence; an edge from $u$ to $v$ of…
nodes.title: Bellman–Ford algorithm

nodes.summary: The cost of a Bellman-Ford run is a pair of natural numbers: the number of edge occurrences checked by relaxation passes, and the number of predecessor edges read or emitted while reconstructing a negative-cycle witness.
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford cost counters

nodes.summary: For a graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, the output of a successful Bellman-Ford run consists of a source vertex $s$, for every vertex a distance that is either an integer or $\infty$, and for every vertex an optional predecessor edge (a weighted directed edge, or none).
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford distance table

nodes.summary: For a list $E$ of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and vertices $u$, $v$, the graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting weights has an edge from $u$ to $v$ if and only if some edge in $E$ has source $u$ and target $v$.
nodes.title: Edges of the weight-forgetting graph

nodes.summary: A weighted directed edge on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ consists of a source vertex, a target vertex and an integer weight.
nodes.title: Weighted directed edge

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and $s$ a vertex. Then $E$ has a negative cycle reachable from $s$ when there is a reachable negative cycle witness for $E$ and $s$: a base vertex $b$, a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $b$ that visits no vertex twice, and a nonempty weighted path in $E$ from $b$ to $b$ whose edge sources are pairwise distinct and whose total weight is…
nodes.title: Existence of a reachable negative cycle

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and let $s$, $m$ and $t$ be vertices. If $P$ is a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $m$ and $e$ is an edge belonging to $E$ with source $m$ and target $t$, then the list $P$ followed by $e$ is a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $t$.
nodes.title: Appending an edge to a weighted path

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices. If the list consisting of an edge $e$ followed by a list $R$ of edges is a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $t$, then $R$ is a weighted path in $E$ from the target of $e$ to $t$.
nodes.title: Tail of a weighted path

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices. If a list $P$ of $k$ edges is a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $t$, then there is a walk of length $k$ from $s$ to $t$ in the directed graph obtained from $E$ by forgetting the weights.
nodes.title: Weighted paths give walks of the same length

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$. A list $P = (e_1, \dots, e_k)$ of weighted directed edges is a weighted path in $E$ from $s$ to $t$ when every $e_i$ belongs to $E$, the target of $e_i$ is the source of $e_{i+1}$ for every $i < k$, and either $k = 0$ and $s = t$, or $k \ge 1$, the source of $e_1$ is $s$ and the target of $e_k$ is $t$.
nodes.title: Weighted path in an edge list

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a distances record on $n$ vertices with source $s$, distance table $d$ (each $d(v)$ is an integer or infinite) and predecessor table $p$; let $E$ be a list of weighted edges; and let $r$ assign to each vertex $v$ a natural number $r(v) < n$. Suppose that $d(s) = 0$, that every vertex $v$ with $d(v)$ infinite has no predecessor, that every vertex $v \ne s$ with $d(v)$ finite has a predecessor, and that…
nodes.title: Predecessor paths realize the distances under a decreasing rank

nodes.summary: Let the output of a Bellman-Ford run on $n$ vertices have source $s$. The path to a vertex $t$ is built backwards from $t$: at a vertex $v \ne s$, take the recorded predecessor edge $e$ of $v$, put it in front of the edges collected so far, and continue from the source of $e$. When $s$ is reached within at most $n$ such steps, the result is the collected list of edges (empty if $t = s$). If some vertex on the way…
nodes.title: Bellman-Ford path reconstruction

nodes.summary: For a vertex $s$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a list of weighted edges $e_1, \dots, e_k$ on these vertices, the vertices of the path from $s$ along this list are the list $s, t_1, \dots, t_k$, where $t_i$ is the target of $e_i$.
nodes.title: Vertices of a path

nodes.summary: For every list $P$ of weighted directed edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and every weighted directed edge $e$ on these vertices, the weight of the list $P$ followed by $e$ is the weight of $P$ plus the weight of $e$.
nodes.title: Weight of a path with an edge appended

nodes.summary: The weight of a list of integer-weighted edges is the sum of the weights of its entries, an edge occurring several times being counted each time.
nodes.title: Bellman–Ford path weight

nodes.summary: For a list of weighted edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and vertices $s$ and $t$, the vertex $t$ is reachable from $s$ in the directed graph obtained from the list by forgetting the weights if and only if there is a weighted path from $s$ to $t$ using edges of the list.
nodes.title: Reachability by weighted paths

nodes.summary: For a list of weighted edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a source vertex $s$, a reachable negative cycle consists of a base vertex $b$, a weighted path $p$ from $s$ to $b$ using edges of the list whose vertices along $p$ from $s$ are pairwise distinct, and a nonempty weighted path $c$ from $b$ to $b$ using edges of the list whose edges have pairwise distinct sources and whose weight is negative.
nodes.title: Reachable negative cycle witness

nodes.summary: For a list of weighted edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a source vertex $s$, a Bellman–Ford result is either a distance record (a source vertex, an optional integer distance for each vertex and an optional predecessor edge for each vertex) or a reachable negative cycle witness for the list and $s$.
nodes.title: Bellman–Ford result

nodes.summary: For a list of weighted edges on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the associated ordered directed graph enumerates its vertices as $0, 1, \dots, n-1$, and the outgoing neighbor list of a vertex $u$ is the list of targets of the edges of the list with source $u$, in the order in which they occur and with repetitions.
nodes.title: Weight-forgetting directed graph

nodes.summary: The total of a Bellman–Ford cost record is its number of edge relaxation checks plus its number of negative-cycle witness reconstruction steps.
nodes.title: Total Bellman–Ford cost
Computer Science

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
